✶The Ledger✶

Days away
321
The carrier USS Abraham Lincoln and its 4,500-plus sailors got home to San Diego Thursday after 321 days away, a record stretch of unbroken time at sea supporting the Iran war. Families met them on the pier.

✶The National Wire✶

1

Isaias Takes Aim at the Gulf Coast

The first Atlantic hurricane of the year is forecast to strengthen to Category 3 before landfall somewhere between Mississippi and the Florida Panhandle. Forecasters expect heavy rain and possible flash flooding.

2

Navi Pillay Wins the Nobel Peace Prize

The South African human rights lawyer and former international judge was honored for advancing human rights and international law. She served on the International Criminal Court, which the Trump administration sanctioned last year.

3

Army Report on the D.C. Midair Crash

The Army's review of the January 2025 collision of an Army helicopter and an American Airlines jet over the Potomac, which killed 67, found failures in air traffic control, helicopter routes, training and safety practices, and called for fixes. It was finished in May and released Thursday after pressure from victims' families.

4

Teen Chatbot Safeguards Fall Short

A Common Sense Media study found most of the safeguards in ChatGPT for Teens failed its tests. Among the gaps: the bot doesn't alert parents when a teen talks about self-harm.

☑ The Ballot · 25 days to Election Day · mailing a ballot late? Get it postmarked at the post office counter so it isn't rejected · register by Oct 24

⛪The Home Wire⛪

1

Rochester · A NASA Telescope Built Here

NASA picked L3Harris to design, build and test a telescope for LISA, a space mission to detect ripples in space-time, and the company says the work will be done in Rochester. The mission is led by the European Space Agency.

2

Fredonia · New School Playgrounds Open

Both Wheelock school playgrounds are finished: Chestnut Street opened in late September and Main Street on Oct. 7. Construction delays had pushed the work into the school year.

3

North Tonawanda · New Charge in Car Show Crash

Charles Brancato, 73, of Tonawanda was arraigned Thursday on a charge of second-degree vehicular assault, North Tonawanda police said. Eight people were hurt when his car went into the crowd at a September car show.

★The Marquee★

1

Avatar: Seven Havens Arrives

The creators of The Last Airbender are back with a new Paramount+ series set after The Legend of Korra. Variety calls its postapocalyptic turn intriguing; The Hollywood Reporter, promising.

2

The Coven Returns

Jessica Lange, Sarah Paulson and the Coven cast are back for the 13th season of FX's American Horror Story. Ryan Murphy lured some of them back after years away, just in time for Halloween.

3

Gromit Speaks

Martin Freeman will voice Gromit, Wallace's famously silent dog, in the audiobook of Gromit's autobiography. It's the first time the character has ever spoken.

🏈The Gridiron🏈

Three Days to Los Angeles
Bills · The Rams come in 2–2, splitting their last two: a 30–26 loss at Denver, then a 24–20 win at Philadelphia. Buffalo is 3–1 and still first in the AFC East.
Jets · Cleveland's 3–1 has them tied with Baltimore atop the AFC North, so Sunday is a real test at home. A win gets the Jets back in the mix.
Thursday night · Tampa Bay 24, Dallas 16, an upset: the Bucs went in with about a 1-in-5 chance.

⚑The Chase⚑

Two Days to Charlotte
Five drivers sit within 84 points of Larson going to Charlotte: Hamlin, Bell, Logano, Blaney and Chase Briscoe. Tyler Reddick has the most wins of the 16 this year, five, but sits seventh, 106 back. Sunday is the sixth of 10 races; most points at Homestead on Nov. 8 takes the title.

☾On This Day☾

October 9, 1888 — The Washington Monument opened to the public. Workers had set its capstone four years earlier, and at 555 feet it was then the tallest structure in the world.

I turn without moving, fall without getting hurt, and get raked into a pile every October. What am I? Answer below the fold.
Question of the Day: A leaf.
